> 節。亨。苦節不可貞。

Hexagram 60 is about limits, and its character is a bamboo joint — which is not primarily a restriction.

## 節 is 竹約 — the joint in bamboo

說文: 節，竹約也 — the binding of bamboo, the node.

Bamboo has joints so that it can grow tall: each segment tightens, and that is where the stiffness comes from.

So 節 was never "restriction." It is structure. Without joints, bamboo is a soft tube lying on the ground.

Which reframes the whole hexagram: the question is not how tight the limit is, but whether the limit is load-bearing.

## 戶庭 and 門庭

戶: the single-leaf inner door (說文 戶，護也，半門曰戶).
門: the two-leaf outer gate.

戶 is inside, 門 is outside.

初九 不出戶庭，無咎 — staying inside the inner door, no fault.
九二 不出門庭，凶 — not going out of the outer gate, and it is bad.

One inside, one outside, opposite verdicts. And that one character is the whole mechanism of the chapter: the same restraint, held one door too long, becomes the failure.

## 嗟 is a breath

嗟: to sigh. Not to weep — the one breath that comes out.

六三 不節若，則嗟若，無咎 — if there is no limit, then there is a sigh; no fault. The line does not condemn the failure; it just records what follows it.

## 甘 and 苦

甘: sweet, the pleasant of the five flavours.
苦: bitter, the unpleasant.

And here they are not tastes. They are whether the limit is bearable — the same measure of restraint, sweet to one person and bitter to another.

Which is the judgement's argument: 苦節不可貞 — a bitter limit cannot be held to. Not because it is wrong, but because it will not last.

## 上六 苦節，貞凶，悔亡

The top line: a bitter limit, held, is 凶 — and the regret is gone.

Which is a hard ending: the one who held too hard loses, and there is nothing left to regret, because the choice was made knowingly.

## 制數度

The 象: 君子以制數度，議德行.

數: to count. 度: the standard, the measure (說文 度，法制也).

So: fix the numbers and the measures.

Not "set limits on oneself." Establish the ruler by which limits will be read — because a limit that cannot be measured cannot be judged sweet or bitter.

## The test

Take a rule you keep — a budget, a working hour, a thing you do not say. Ask which door it is at: the inner one or the outer one. The hexagram's judgement does not turn on severity. It turns on whether the restraint is still protecting something, or whether it has started protecting nothing.
